newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU ministers to ponder kerosene tax options.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers to ponder kerosene tax options.

text.p: European Union transport ministers will consider next Tuesday a Dutch plan to research the effects of lifting existing EU tax exemptions for aviation fuel, a Dutch diplomat told a Friday news conference.

The Dutch, who hold the EU's sixth-month presidency, want ministers to back a resolution asking the European Commission to study the effects of introducing a kerosene tax as a prelude to a possible scrapping of the exemption at the end of 1997.
"These exemptions are increasingly being criticised due to concerns about the adverse environmental effects of expanding air traffic," one EU official said on Friday.

European Union environment ministers said in December 1994 that the exclusion of commercial aviation from excise duties was unjustified on environmental grounds, a point raised by the Austrians at an environment ministers' meeting this week.
Critics say that unilateral introduction of such measures for EU carriers would put them at a disadvantage relative to their international competitors.
Imposing taxes could also cause legal complications, as the exemption is written into various international and bilateral aviation agreements.
